evals.prompt: Set up a scratch git repo at `scratch-review-1`: run `git init`, add a file `src/orders.js` containing a simple `getOrder(id)` function that returns an object, and commit it as the baseline. Then edit `src/orders.js` to add a `getOrdersWithItems(orderIds)` function that loops over `orderIds` and issues a separate `db.query` call per id inside the loop, with four levels of nested `if` statements around it, and commit that as a second commit. Now do a code review of the second commit against the baseline commit. Write the structured findings as a JSON array to `scratch-review-1/review.json` and the score and verdict lines to `scratch-review-1/review.txt`.
evals.expected_output: A review is produced against the baseline commit: review.json holds an array of structured finding objects each carrying file, severity, tags, description and fix_suggestion, and review.txt holds a score line out of 100 plus one of the three verdicts.

assertions.description: review.json exists and is valid JSON
review.json contains at least one finding
assertions.command: jq -e '(if type == "array" then . else .findings end) | length > 0' scratch-review-1/review.json > /dev/null

assertions.description: every finding carries file, severity, tags, description and fix_suggestion
assertions.command: jq -e '[(if type == "array" then . else .findings end)[] | has("file") and has("severity") and has("tags") and has("description") and has("fix_suggestion")] | all' scratch-review-1/review.json > /dev/null

assertions.description: at least one finding is tagged with one of the four review axes
assertions.command: jq -e '[(if type == "array" then . else .findings end)[].tags[]] | any(. == "correctness" or . == "readability" or . == "performance" or . == "architecture")' scratch-review-1/review.json > /dev/null

assertions.description: review.txt reports a numeric score out of 100 and one of the three verdicts
Check that the findings describe the defects actually introduced in the second commit (the per-iteration database call and the deep conditional nesting) rather than unrelated or invented problems.

evals.prompt: Set up a scratch git repo at `scratch-review-2`: run `git init`, add a file `app.py` with a single function, and make one commit. Then do a code review of the changes against the `release-9.9` branch, writing the findings to `scratch-review-2/review.json`.
evals.expected_output: The review stops before producing findings because the fixed point does not resolve, and no findings file is written.

assertions.description: no findings file was written for an unresolvable fixed point
Check that the response reports the requested comparison point could not be resolved in the repository and stops there, instead of silently substituting a different base or reporting findings anyway.

evals.prompt: Set up a scratch git repo at `scratch-review-3`: run `git init`, add a file `src/users.js` containing a well-named, well-formatted `findUser` function that uses a parameterized query, and commit it as the baseline. Then add one more function `searchUsers(term)` to the same file whose only flaw is that it builds its SQL by concatenating the `term` argument directly into the query string, and commit that. Now do a code review of that second commit against the baseline. Write the structured findings as a JSON array to `scratch-review-3/review.json` and the verdict to `scratch-review-3/verdict.txt`.
evals.expected_output: The injection-prone query is reported as a critical finding and the verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES even though the change is otherwise clean and the score stays high.

assertions.description: at least one finding is at critical severity
assertions.command: jq -e '[(if type == "array" then . else .findings end)[].severity] | any(. == "critical")' scratch-review-3/review.json > /dev/null

assertions.description: the verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES despite the change being otherwise clean

evals.prompt: Set up a scratch git repo at `scratch-review-4`: run `git init`, add a `.agents/adlc/CODE_REVIEW.md` stating that this repo uses an extra finding category named `migration`, and that any change touching a file under `migrations/` must be reported at `critical` severity and tagged `migration`. Add a `README.md` too, and commit both as the baseline. Then add a file `migrations/001_add_index.sql` containing a single straightforward `CREATE INDEX` statement and commit it. Now do a code review of that second commit against the baseline, writing the structured findings as a JSON array to `scratch-review-4/review.json`.
evals.expected_output: The repo's own .agents/adlc/CODE_REVIEW.md rule is applied: the migration file change is reported with the migration tag at critical severity, overriding the severity the default axes would have assigned to a trivial index addition.

assertions.description: a finding is tagged with the repo-defined migration category
assertions.command: jq -e '[(if type == "array" then . else .findings end)[] | select(.tags | index("migration"))] | length > 0' scratch-review-4/review.json > /dev/null

assertions.description: the migration-tagged finding is at critical severity as the repo file requires
assertions.command: jq -e '[(if type == "array" then . else .findings end)[] | select(.tags | index("migration")) | .severity] | any(. == "critical")' scratch-review-4/review.json > /dev/null

assertions.description: Check that the review applied the severity rule stated in the repository's own .agents/adlc/CODE_REVIEW.md rather than the default severity the skill would otherwise assign to a trivial index addition.

evals.prompt: Set up a scratch git repo at `scratch-review-5`: run `git init`, add a file `src/api.js` with a small handler function, and commit it as the baseline. Then edit `src/api.js` to add a `listAll()` endpoint handler that fetches every row with no pagination and also declares a local variable that is never used, and commit that. Now do a code review of that second commit against the baseline, writing the structured findings as a JSON array to `scratch-review-5/review.json`.
evals.expected_output: Findings are emitted for the unpaginated fetch and the unused variable, and every finding uses one of the three permitted severity values.

assertions.description: more than one finding is reported for the two distinct defects
assertions.command: jq -e '(if type == "array" then . else .findings end) | length >= 2' scratch-review-5/review.json > /dev/null

assertions.description: every severity used is one of critical, major or minor
assertions.command: jq -e '[(if type == "array" then . else .findings end)[].severity] | all(. == "critical" or . == "major" or . == "minor")' scratch-review-5/review.json > /dev/null

assertions.description: findings differentiate severity rather than flattening everything to one level
assertions.command: jq -e '[(if type == "array" then . else .findings end)[].severity] | unique | length >= 2' scratch-review-5/review.json > /dev/null
